title: add CI artifact signing, SBOM and provenance release manifests for private-installer
author: Priya Singh
description: This PR adds end-to-end release automation for the private-installer artifacts: build pipelines now emit signed release artifacts, SBOMs, and provenance manifests/attestations to support verifiable on-prem installs. Motivation: regulated customers and offline/private installs require cryptographic provenance, reproducible SBOMs, and a release manifest that ties installer bundles to build metadata. What this PR does: adds a new build job (actions/ci/release-private-installer.yml) that produces tarballs and Helm charts, generates SPDX SBOMs via syft, produces a provenance.yaml and an in-toto statement signed with KMS/GPG, uploads artifacts to the release bucket alongside a signature (.sig) and a provenance manifest (.prov.yaml), exposes a signing-key-rotation test matrix, and wires these artifacts into the existing release-manifests generator so release pages show artifact checksums, sbom links, and provenance attestations. Checklist: - [x] CI job that builds and packages installer artifacts; - [x] SBOM generation and upload; - [x] Artifact signing (KMS wrapper with optional local GPG fallback); - [x] Generate provenance manifests (in-toto compatible) and upload; - [x] Update release-manifests generator and templates; - [x] Integration test for offline verification flow; - [x] Documentation updates and release notes. Backwards compatibility: artifacts are still produced in existing locations and the new .sig/.prov.yaml/.sbom.json files are additive; installers that don't verify signatures are unaffected. Key implementation notes: we implemented a small signing-wrapper script scripts/sign-artifact.sh that supports KMS-based signing and local GPG for CI runners, added step to pipeline to notarize artifacts with sha256 checksums, and migrated the release-manifests generator to include an artifacts[].provenance_url and artifacts[].sbom_url fields in emitted manifest YAML. See files changed for details. Security: signing keys are referenced from secrets:KMS_KEY_NAME and the CI job enforces least-privilege roles for the service account. Observability: build metadata (build_id, git_ref, image_digest) are embedded in provenance manifests and surfaced in release metadata. Release notes: Adds verifiable signed artifacts and SBOMs for private-installer releases, improving auditability and offline install security.
commits: feat(ci): add release pipeline for private-installer with SBOM and signing
chore(signing): add scripts/sign-artifact.sh KMS + GPG support
feat(provenance): emit in-toto-compatible provenance manifests and upload alongside artifacts
test(ci): add integration test for signature verification and sbom validation
docs(release): document verification steps for offline installs
diff_snippets:
+ name: Build and sign private-installer artifacts  uses: ./.github/actions/build-packages steps:
  - name: Build packages
  - name: Generate SBOM (syft)
  - name: Sign artifact (KMS/GPG fallback)
  - name: Upload artifacts and provenance

+ # scripts/sign-artifact.sh  +#!/usr/bin/env bash +set -euo pipefail +if [[ -n "$KMS_KEY_NAME" ]]; then gcloud kms sign --key=$KMS_KEY_NAME --input=$1 --output=${1}.sig; else gpg --batch --yes --output ${1}.sig --sign $1; fi
+ release-manifests/generator.py: include 'provenance_url' and 'sbom_url' when present so UI can show verification links
review_comments: Ethan Park: Please confirm KMS key rotation behavior and add a unit test for key rotation in the signing wrapper.
Priya Singh (author): Added a signing key rotation matrix to the CI job and included a small test that exercises KMS key rotation emulation. See ci/integ/verify-offline-install.sh changes.
Maya Chen: Integration test flakes on first run (timeout in verification). Can we increase the wait and add retries?
Priya Singh: Increased verification timeout and added exponential retry in the test harness. Reran CI.
Carlos Rivera: Security review: ensure KMS keys are not leaked to PR forks. Confirmed CI job only runs on protected branches; for forks we fall back to local GPG in gated runs.
Ethan Park: LGTM after docs and small nits addressed.
notes_to_release: Private-installer releases now publish signed artifacts (.sig), provenance manifests (.prov.yaml), and SBOMs (.sbom.json). Users performing offline or air-gapped installs can verify artifact integrity and provenance. This is additive and backwards-compatible. See docs/private-installer/release-verification.md for verification steps and key rotation guidance.
release_notes: Add signed artifacts, SBOMs, and provenance manifests to private-installer releases to enable verifiable offline installs and stronger auditability.
post_merge_actions: docs: publish release-verification.md to docs site
security_considerations: Signing uses customer CI KMS credentials referenced via secrets; CI jobs that run on forks use a local GPG fallback and do not have access to KMS. Key rotation matrix added to integration tests. Least-privilege IAM role required for the service account used by release CI.
user_impact: No breaking changes for existing installs. New artifacts (signature, sbom, provenance) are optional and used by customers who opt into verification. Documentation included for verification steps.
notes: This PR consolidates prior work and completes the end-to-end flow for signed/private-installer releases. Follow-up work: add OCI registry attestations and integrate with SLSA attestations pipeline.
